verdicts.claim: By default SQLite checkpoints automatically after a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more ... SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT changes the 1000-page default
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages. (The SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to specify a different default.)'

verdicts.claim: SQLite 3.51.0 (2025-11-04) added PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument to sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2()
verdicts.evidence: changes.html '2025-11-04 (3.51.0)' section: 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument'; pragma.html: 'NOOP This mode does not checkpoint any frames. It is used to obtain the returned values only.'

verdicts.claim: WAL-reset bug likely present in every release from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09) and is fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later'; changes.html '2026-03-13 (3.51.3) Fix the WAL-reset database corruption bug.'

verdicts.claim: The 3.53.0 notes (2026-04-09) list the fix too. Release 3.52.0 (2026-03-06) is marked withdrawn ... newest release 3.54.1 (2026-10-16)
verdicts.evidence: changes.html: '2026-04-09 (3.53.0) Fix the WAL-reset database corruption bug.'; '2026-03-06 (3.52.0) Withdrawn All of the features ... moved forward into version 3.53.0'; top entry '2026-10-16 (3.54.1)'

verdicts.claim: The default journal_size_limit is -1, which means no limit
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit).'

verdicts.claim: When the last connection closes, SQLite runs one final checkpoint and deletes the WAL file. SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE ... positive value disables it
verdicts.evidence: dbconfig: 'SQLite performs a checkpoint before closing the connection and deletes the WAL file ... integer which is positive to disable checkpoints-on-close'

verdicts.claim: Firefox compiles in SQLITE_DEFAULT_JOURNAL_SIZE_LIMIT = 1572864 bytes (1.5 MiB), and its Places database uses 4 MiB ... truncated instead of deleted
verdicts.evidence: commit: "DEFINES['SQLITE_DEFAULT_JOURNAL_SIZE_LIMIT'] = 1572864"; 'but Places that is using a larger 4MiB limit ... they will be truncated instead of deleted'. Sub-claim 'still sets wal_autocheckpoint per database' not checked.

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(RESTART) returns SQLITE_BUSY almost instantly ... another checkpoint already running ... Fix: PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0 on every connection
verdicts.evidence: Dan Kennedy: 'If there is another checkpointer running, sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() will return SQLITE_BUSY immediately. It only uses the busy handler for database readers and writers'; Crawshaw: 'Setting PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0; on every connection resolves the issue'

verdicts.claim: Litestream keeps a long-running read transaction open so that no other process can checkpoint and restart the WAL ... calls SQLite itself to checkpoint
verdicts.evidence: how-it-works: 'It starts a long-running read transaction to prevent any other process from checkpointing and restarting the WAL file. Instead, it continually reads new WAL pages and manually calls out to SQLite to perform checkpoints'

verdicts.claim: SQLite describes the WAL-reset bug as rare ... Phil Eaton supplied a reproducer that needs none, and the page says the bug is not an emergency
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'UPDATE: 2026-08-24 → Phil Eaton has devised a reproducer that does not involve using the special testing code hack'; 'this is not an emergency'. Antithesis/Register sub-quotes not separately checked.
